clue.text: Extended passage of river in boat …

indicators.note: in tells us the river abbreviation sits inside the word for the boat

parts.note: a galley is an oared ship
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A long stretch of river travelled in a boat, the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 5 across, whose theatre sense of a top gallery joins the two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can be a long covered corridor or walkway, so an extended passage fits.

clue.text: Opening of musical first to last with cry of approval

indicators.note: the first letter of the show's name is moved to the end

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
ole is the Spanish cheer of approval

explanation.surface: A show's premiere, running start to finish, greeted with cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: An air hole is a small opening that lets air in or out.

clue.text: Man, say, after end of doleful yarn

indicators.note: after puts the island piece behind the letter
end of picks out the final letter of doleful

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man telling a gloomy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale but is thread: lisle is a fine cotton thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings.

clue.text: Gold aroused fever in country

indicators.note: in a down clue roused upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
mania is a frenzy or fever of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Gold rush fever stirring in a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: … whose lap holds the future

parts.note: the idiom says what is uncertain lies 'in the lap of' the deities; read on from 1 across it also names the top gallery of a theatre

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across, a river journey whose outcome rests with fate.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the highest, cheapest gallery is nicknamed after the deities, which ties this clue to the theme of galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the lap of the deities' means the outcome is beyond human control, resting with heavenly powers.

clue.text: Man of aesthetic tastes — bogus? Sincere

parts.note: he is a man
arty describes someone with pretentious, rather bogus artistic tastes

explanation.surface: Is the aesthete a fake, or genuine?
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford the hearty, a sporting type, was the traditional opposite of the aesthete, so the surface points the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty welcome is warm and sincere, heartfelt.

clue.text: Acquired old dosh for a holy man with speed

parts.note: got means acquired
oof is old slang for money
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: Someone got cash for a saint in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To go too fast is to move with excessive speed, so the phrase describes speeding.

clue.text: Stupid person, appropriately short and fat

indicators.note: short means losing the final letter

parts.note: the setter uses this to stand for the word fitting a stupid person, dull
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A dim person who, fittingly, is short and plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriately' gives the adjective that suits a stupid person, cut short by 'short', followed by the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted, dim person.

clue.text: The accented and expensive professeur

parts.note: the French word professeur names a schoolteacher of a language full of accents, and cher, French for expensive, ends the second word

explanation.surface: A costly teacher with a strong accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A professeur teaching his language would be a teacher of the Gallic tongue.

clue.text: See 16
Trading company leader opposed to be eaten by blackbird

indicators.note: being eaten by the bird means going inside its name

parts.note: merle is an old Scots and poetic name for the blackbird

indicators.note: leader takes only the front letter of the word company

parts.note: anti means against, opposed to

explanation.surface: A firm's boss who objects to being devoured by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trading company' looks like the definition, but 'company' joins 'leader' to give a single letter; 'Trading' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes things concerned with trade and merchants.

clue.text: 1 after 27, the fashion for sailors

parts.note: the mode is the current style or fashion
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Seemingly a fashion item made for a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 after 27' means the gallery word that follows 27 across's first word: the London gallery of modern art on Bankside.
explanation.definitionFit: London's gallery of modern art on Bankside carries this word after the name of 27 across.

clue.text: 1, the race of the race?

definitions.meaning: the theme word: the London gallery in Trafalgar Square
the Grand steeplechase at Aintree is the race, and the adjective also means belonging to a nation or people

explanation.definitionFit: The Trafalgar Square gallery and the Aintree steeplechase both bear the name; the adjective means of a people or nation.

clue.text: Leaves the Basque revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters of the phrase are turned about

explanation.surface: A Basque uprising leaves the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like departure but is the verb for passing things on by will.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to leave property to someone in a will.

clue.text: Floor covering was insufficiently sensitive

definitions.meaning: a felt layer laid under carpets
read as two words: experienced too little feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Underfelt is a carpet underlay; split, the words mean felt too little.

clue.text: Mess up excavation of painter before the end of 7

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
a dig is an archaeological excavation
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter; 'of painter' is the possessive RA'S

explanation.surface: Ruining a painter's dig before the close of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down ends with the word for abstaining from food; the Tuesday carnival comes just before the Lenten abstinence begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday's carnival falls on the day before Lent, the season of fasting, begins.

clue.text: 1 giving trouble to priest

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A gallery causing bother for a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the national art museum in Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is one of the world's great art galleries.

clue.text: Beast that lays eggs on rising grass

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An animal laying eggs on grass that grows upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer, a wild animal.

clue.text: 1 spot for loner married in the past that's still with us?

indicators.note: in tells us the married abbreviation goes inside the word for inherited past

parts.words: the past that's still with us?
parts.note: heritage is the inheritance of the past that survives into the present

explanation.surface: A recluse's retreat, once married, preserving the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: the State museum in St Petersburg is a gallery, and a recluse's home is a spot for a loner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit's dwelling suits a loner, and the Hermitage in St Petersburg is a famous art museum.

clue.text: A goal up, during which I gave fire to fighting men

indicators.note: during which places the next pieces inside the reversed goal
in a down clue up reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: an aim is a goal
lit means set alight

explanation.surface: Fighting men lighting a fire after aiming high.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers, men who fight.

clue.text: A strong inclination to be somewhere near John Lennon

indicators.note: an inclination is a bent, and bent letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strong urge to be near a Beatle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a district of Liverpool beside Liverpool John Lennon Airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool district lies next to the airport named after the Beatle.

clue.text: 1 sees endless effervescence in topless mystic

indicators.note: in places the bubbles inside the mystic
topless removes the first letter

parts.note: a Sufi is a Muslim mystic

indicators.note: endless removes the last letter

parts.note: fizz is bubbling effervescence

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor sees bubbles in a half-dressed mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Florence's great art gallery, beside the Arno.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence is one of the world's most famous art galleries.

clue.text: Tremendous quantity of land provided for price of 26

parts.note: Terr. is the abbreviation for territory, an area of land
if means provided that
the small price in 26 across is one cent, written I and C

explanation.surface: A huge amount of land given away cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 26 across ends with a small price, one cent; written as I plus C for cent it gives the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific is an informal synonym of tremendous, both meaning very great.

clue.text: 1 opening

definitions.meaning: the theme word: the celebrated Paris museum and gallery
a ventilating opening fitted with slanting slats

explanation.definitionFit: The great Paris museum is a gallery; the same word names a slatted ventilation opening.

clue.text: Speak without qualification

definitions.meaning: complete, absolute, as in total nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Utter means to say aloud, and also means complete or absolute.

clue.text: Kind of meat without name at small price

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the meat surrounds the name abbreviation

parts.note: beef is meat from cattle
one cent, written I for one plus CENT, is a small price

explanation.surface: An unnamed cheap cut of meat on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of meat' looks like a definition of a cut; 'Kind' alone is the adjective. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneficent means doing good to others, a synonym of kind and generous.

clue.text: 1 time antipyretic suppressing sex appeal first

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so the drug name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Atebrin is a trade name for mepacrine, a drug used against malarial fever
it is old slang for sex appeal
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A fever drug that dampens desire, taken at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Atebrin (mepacrine) is an old antimalarial that brings fever down. The answer is the London gallery of British art on Millbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate Britain is a national art gallery in London, so the theme word fits.

clue.text: See 27
Having no fixed abode, I abandon source of potency for books

indicators.note: abandon tells us the letter I is dropped from the drug name

parts.note: Viagra is a drug taken for sexual potency
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A homeless person gives up a performance drug in favour of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I abandon' tells us the letter I leaves the drug's name, which leaves VAGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a wanderer with no settled home.
